subject: Turning drawings into manufactured components
hook: One cutting list, three machines, a stack of labelled parts.
ig:
One cutting list, three machines, a stack of labelled parts.

This is how a trade order moves through our Hanley workshop.

The sliding table panel saw cuts each part to the finished size on your list. The edge bander applies ABS edging to the edges you specified, in 0.4, 1 or 2 mm. The multi-spindle boring machine drills hinge cups, shelf-pin rows and dowel holes. Every part is referenced so it matches your list when it lands on your bench.

From there you can collect from the workshop, have it delivered, or ask us to assemble the cabinets too.

It suits joiners and fitters who would rather spend their time installing than processing board.

Want the trade services page? Comment PANELS and we will send it over.
fb:
Ever wondered what happens to your cutting list once it reaches us?

This is the route through our Hanley workshop: cut on the sliding table panel saw, edged on the edge bander, drilled on the multi-spindle boring machine, then labelled and stacked so every part matches your list. You can collect, have it delivered, or let us assemble the carcasses as well.

If you are a joiner, fitter or small maker with board processing eating into your week, this is the bit we can take off your hands.
